hazards.label: Heat
hazards.effect_note: The twin's heat leads (ageing, derating, chiller capacity) work through performance, not physical damage; pointer to the outage-as-performance work, no curve (discussion 04 §6).

hazards.label: Icing
hazards.effect_note: Two leads in the twin: snow load on the venting panels (physical, L) and cold limiting the charge rate until heated (performance, L). No hazard cell; the C-172 snow-and-ice reasoning applies (discussion 04 §6).

hazards.label: Lightning
hazards.effect_note: No hazard cell exists; the twin carries Medium surge leads on the electronics (discussion 04 §6).

tier_meaning.T1: field-calibrated: fitted to insurance claims or field damage surveys of the same kind of asset

tier_meaning.T3: borrowed: from a similar asset or a related study, with an engineering step to make it fit
tier_meaning.T4: our judgment: no source gives the number; a placeholder until evidence replaces it

Heat: define the consequence before building the model (Hazard, 21 Oct 2026): Parked by the owner on 21 Oct: temporary derating, permanent ageing and acute failure need separate definitions, and working cooling should be compared with impaired cooling. No owner ruling yet. Damage's scope: a damage curve prices physical destruction only: Heat is treated as changing how an asset performs (derating, ageing), which sits outside a damage curve; disruption and derating are a separate stage. Does it happen? Hazard multiplies PV_MODULE_GLASS_CELL by 35.54% of installed value (PV module hardware plus replacement fieldwork: $398,084 / $1,120,000, runtime-rounded to 0.3554); the artifact shown here declares 26.00% of installed capex.

status.meaning: Finished and in use: the platform's loss calculations can use this curve today.
status.catalogue: In the runtime artifact index (docs/contracts/machine_readable_artifact_index.json); the platform can call it

status.meaning: Built and checked, but not in use yet: it waits for an owner's review before the platform can use it.
status.catalogue: Built and validated in the repository but not in the runtime index; waiting for review

status.meaning: No curve of its own: it borrows a live curve built for another asset, which its page names (for example, a substation borrows the substation part of a solar farm's curve).
status.catalogue: No curve of its own; a consumer binding prices this asset with another cell's curve

status.meaning: Nothing has been built for this asset and hazard yet; its page says why and lists the research so far.
Part of the asset's value has no curve yet.

coverage.meaning: A curve is built for this subsystem itself.
A curve covers only part of this subsystem; the rest has none.
No curve of its own, but not left out: the hazard prices the whole building with one curve, and this subsystem's damage is inside it (hail is the exception, with its own roof and walls curves).
No curve covers this subsystem; the row says why and links the research.
No curve of its own: its condition (for example whether a protection is in place) changes another part's curve.

Judged not to be damaged directly by this hazard: by the cell's own coverage decision, or, where the cell is silent, read from how the hazard acts (to confirm with the cell owner; the part's note says which).
Left out of the value this curve prices (for example contents, modeled separately).

completeness.meaning: This part's share of the asset's value: of its reference plant's value budget where the asset has one, else the share the cell's own units declare (hover for the basis).

value.meaning: A curve prices this hazard's damage to these parts, or the cell adds their cost in step with the other parts' damage (replacement labour).
A curve covers only some of these parts (for example wildfire on a substation, whose curve covers the yard equipment but not the rest of each subsystem).
The cell judged this hazard does not damage these parts directly, so a loss of $0 there is right, not missing.
No curve, so any damage to these parts is not counted in the loss.

value.word: no value budget for buildings yet
value.meaning: Real estate has no budget splitting a building's value into its parts, so the split cannot be worked out; each curve is a share of the building's replacement cost, which the consumer supplies.

evidence.meaning: fitted to insurance claims or field damage surveys of the same kind of asset
taken from a published standard, a public model such as FEMA Hazus, lab tests or physics
from a similar asset or a related study, with an engineering step to make it fit
no source gives the number; a placeholder until evidence replaces it

production.meaning: Damage has signed this curve off for Hazard: it is on Damage's list of released curves, so Hazard's software is allowed to load it. Whether Hazard's maps already use it is the next tag, Used by Hazard.
Released, but as another asset's curve: the platform prices this asset with a curve built for something else.
Not signed off for Hazard yet (a proposal): it is not on Damage's list of released curves, so Hazard's software should not load it.

hazard_use.meaning: A layer on Hazard's internal dashboard was computed with this file, or one identical to it in everything that can change a loss (curves, value shares, unit treatments).
A layer on Hazard's dashboard was computed with something that differs in a way that can change a loss: a newer model, a changed revision, or a different value share. The note says what.
No layer on Hazard's dashboard uses this cell; the row says whether any Hazard branch holds it.

where_from.borrowed: Borrowed: taken from a similar asset or a related study and adapted.
where_from.our_judgment: Our judgment: no source gives this number.
where_from.curve_level: No source for this number alone: it rests on the curve's own sources.
where_from.unsourced: Set by the team; no source cited.

units.meaning: Hazard × asset pair; project-management unit; e.g. hail × solar, flood × solar
Thing that actually fails; curve-record unit; e.g. PV module glass/cell trigger; inverter inundation
Engineering vocabulary and value-link unit; e.g. PV_ARRAY / PV_MODULE; INVERTER_SYSTEM / INVERTER
Dollar bucket the DR applies to; e.g. Exposed PV module value; inverter value

lenses.meaning: The first line of every tile, and its shade (see a curve's status): what exists for this asset and hazard.
How well supported the curve's numbers are, in one word: the weaker of two grades: the damage at each hazard level, and the dollar value that damage is applied to (hover a tile for both).
Of everything the asset is worth (its reference plant's value budget), how much this hazard's curves price; the parts it is split into are under Value covered below.
Whether a person has reviewed this entry, or only an agent has read it.

marks.meaning: A live curve: the platform can use it.
A proposal: built and checked, not in use yet.
Reused: priced with another cell's curve, not one of its own.
No curve yet for this asset and hazard.
The curves cover only part of the asset's value.
The curve exists but this repository's code cannot draw it.
Darker grey means weaker evidence: clear for field-calibrated or published, darkest for our judgment.
Only an agent has read the entry; no person has reviewed it yet.
